text:
maggie: quick check — can someone run a focused micro-profiling run on int4 vs fp8 for llama-13b, please? need latency/throughput numbers and a small quality delta on the QA eval set. target: keep pass@1 drop <1%.
ben: I can take this, when do you need it and which config? batch sizes? seq len?
dmitri: ping — 
I usually run:
```bash
./bench/run_infer.sh --model llama-13b --quant int4 --batch 1 --seq 512 --iters 200 
```
and then again with --quant fp8. use --seed 42 to be deterministic.
ci-bot: Started job #3942: bench/quant-probe (llama-13b, int4) — logs: https://ci.internal/3942 :gear:
omar: for quality, do you want the full QA harness or just a lightweight EM/accuracy check? full harness is slower.
maggie: lightweight first (EM+F1 on dev-qa ~2k examples) is fine. if delta <1% we can escalate to full eval. thanks.
ben: running int4 now, will post numbers. can someone confirm we should pin to kernel v2.1? new kernels changed perf a bit.
carol: yes pin to v2.1 for now, otherwise results not comparable to last week. use runtime flag RUNTIME_KERNEL=v2.1.
dmitri: note: set KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=1 for fp8 runs; it improves latency on long seqs.
ben: int4 results (quick):
```
Quant: int4 | batch=1 seq=512 | p50=78ms p95=210ms | throughput=12 tok/s | EM=86.1%
Quant: fp8  | batch=1 seq=512 | p50=98ms p95=240ms | throughput=9.5 tok/s | EM=86.9%
```
ben: so EM delta = -0.8% (int4 vs fp8) which is within target. latency improved ~20% at p50.
omar: nice. did you run warmup steps? cold starts change p95 a lot.
ben: yes 50 warmup iters. I noted p95 has some tails, might be GC/host issue — adding traces.
ci-bot: Job #3942 completed successfully :white_check_mark: 
dmitri: re: tails, try disabling host-side prefetch to see if the tail moves — set HOST_PREFETCH=0.
maggie: great work team — can we capture these numbers in the perf tracker? Ben/Carol can you add a short note with commands + env vars used? I'll loop in product for rollout decision. :thumbsup:
carol: adding note to /perf/quant/llama-13b/2026-03-17.md now with the bench command, envs, and raw numbers.
ben: will also attach the raw logs to the report.
maggie: moving to follow-up: if we get consistent numbers across 3 runs, we can put int4 as a candidate default for low-cost tier. if anyone sees a regression on a different eval set please flag it here. :eyes:
